events.title: Introduction of Standard Time Zones in North America
events.description: On this day, known as the 'Day of Two Noons,' U.S. and Canadian railroads adopted four standard continental time zones, replacing hundreds of local solar times. Clocks were reset at noon in many cities as the new system took effect.
events.significance: It standardized timekeeping for railroad scheduling and commerce, paving the way for the Standard Time Act of 1918 and the global system of time zones.

events.title: Premiere of Steamboat Willie
events.description: Walt Disney's short animated film Steamboat Willie premiered at the Colony Theatre in New York City. It was one of the first cartoons with synchronized sound and introduced Mickey Mouse to a wide audience.
events.significance: The film launched Mickey Mouse as a cultural icon and helped establish The Walt Disney Company, setting the course for the modern animation industry.

events.title: Jonestown Massacre
events.description: More than 900 members of the Peoples Temple, led by Jim Jones, died in Jonestown, Guyana, in a mass murder-suicide by cyanide poisoning. Earlier that day, Congressman Leo Ryan and several others were killed at a nearby airstrip.
events.significance: It was the largest single loss of American civilian life in a deliberate act prior to September 11, 2001, and it brought lasting attention to cults and religious extremism.

events.title: Legendary Date of William Tell's Apple Shot
events.description: According to Swiss tradition, William Tell was forced to shoot an apple from his son's head on this date, an act said to have sparked resistance against Habsburg rule. Historians regard the story as legend rather than documented fact.
events.significance: The tale became a foundational national symbol of Swiss independence and resistance to tyranny, though its historicity is disputed.

events.title: Siege of Vukovar Ends
events.description: After a nearly three-month siege, the Croatian city of Vukovar fell to the Yugoslav People's Army and Serb paramilitary forces during the Croatian War of Independence. The city was heavily destroyed, and the aftermath included the Ovčara massacre.
events.significance: The battle became a symbol of Croatian resistance and of the brutality of the Yugoslav wars, and it led to war crimes prosecutions at the international tribunal.
